__comment: Door - the doc 22 prerequisite for doc 34's sealed-room detection.
RESIZED 2026-08-06 (Alen playtest feedback): footprint is 2x1 (was 1x1),
visually 2 blocks wide x 4 blocks tall - the original single-tile slab
read as out-of-proportion next to 3-tall dwarves and 1-wide corridors.
Both footprint cells matter for sealing: RoomManager now registers EVERY
footprint cell a door occupies as a sealing boundary (not just the
origin cell), so a 2-wide door only seals a room if BOTH tiles stop the
flood-fill - see FurniturePlacementController._install/_teardown_installed
passing component.cells (the full footprint) to on_furniture_changed(),
and RoomManager.on_furniture_changed()'s updated 'cells: Array[Vector3i]'
signature.
COLLISION_REGIONS IS DELIBERATELY EMPTY. Every other furniture piece uses
collision_regions to register NavGrid-blocking occupancy (see
FurniturePlacementController._install). A door must stay walkable, so it
carries no occupancy boxes at all - placing one changes nothing about
pathing. It IS still footprint-tracked (blocks a stockpile zone from being
drawn on the same tile, which you wouldn't want anyway) and IS tracked by
RoomManager as a sealing boundary via the direct on_furniture_changed()
call FurniturePlacementController makes on install/uninstall.
Per doc 34: 'Dwarves always close doors behind them. Door blocks are
always treated as sealed for temperature calculation purposes regardless
of animation state.' v1 has no open/close animation at all - every
installed door is permanently 'closed' for sealing purposes, which is a
strict superset of that rule (always-sealed is always at least as sealed
as 'sealed except when a dwarf is mid-walk-through').
PLACEMENT: v1 has no doorway validation (no check that the door sits
between two solid walls) - only the standard NavGrid.is_walkable(cell)
check every floor piece gets. Place doors sensibly; a door in the open
does nothing (RoomManager's flood-fill will simply fail to find a
bounded interior on either side of it).
definition.description: A stout double plank door on iron hinges. Dwarves pass through freely; it seals the room for warmth.
